Consult Summary:
- Acute unilateral left headache with photophobia; differential includes tension-type headache or migraine; plan includes NSAID therapy, lifestyle measures, and follow-up in one week.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Woke this morning with severe left-sided headache; pain persists.
- Onset/duration/progression: Began around 5:30 AM today; ongoing; initial discomfort when lying down, then somewhat soothed; pain worse on waking and persistent.
- Associated symptoms: Light sensitivity (photophobia) present; dizziness earlier but resolved; no neck stiffness; no fever; no significant nausea currently.
- Prior history: History of headaches in the past but none as severe; history of anxiety.
- Medications/Allergies: On sertraline (dose/frequency not documented); acetaminophen (taken this morning; dose/frequency not documented); no other meds noted. Allergies not documented; patient reports none known.
- Social history: Lives with partner; non-smoker; cat at home; exercises by running ~3 times/week; high work stress with late nights for ~2 months.
- Family history: No migraines in family; mother has anxiety; no significant physical illnesses reported.

Examination:
- No physical examination performed or documented.
- No vitals documented.

Impression:
- Possible tension-type headache related to work/stress and anxiety history, with alternative consideration of migraine given unilateral pain and photophobia.

Plan:
- Medications:
  - Ibuprofen started as first-line analgesic for presumed migraine/tension-type headache; dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Acetaminophen may be continued as needed; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Activity/occupational health:
  - Consider taking one week off work (self-certify) to reduce headache burden.
  - Consider counseling options; link for self-referral provided.
- Lifestyle measures:
  - Aim for 7–8 hours sleep per night.
  - Hydration target: 1.5–2 liters of fluids per day (not including caffeine-containing beverages).
- Safety/education:
  - Provide information/link on danger signs of headaches; advised to contact if symptoms worsen or new red flags appear.
- Follow-up:
  - Appointment in 1 week to reassess; if not improving, may pursue blood tests or further evaluation as indicated.
  - If symptoms worsen or concerns arise sooner, contact to arrange earlier reassessment.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vitals and general physical examination findings (not provided).
  - Comprehensive medication reconciliation (only sertraline and acetaminophen noted; other meds not listed).
  - Formal documentation of allergies (patient reports no known allergies; not explicitly documented as formal allergy entry).
- Internal conflicts: None identified.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor conversational filler and routine reassurances; no significant inaudible data.
